summary: The candidate thanks the employer, says they want to think it over, and asks for a few days.
realLife: Career offices advise not accepting on the spot, asking for two days to a week and naming a specific window, often three to five days. If pushed, the candidate explains they want to choose well and asks if the deadline can move a little.
sources: Duke University career blog, how to evaluate a job offer and ask for time: https://careerhub.students.duke.edu/blog/2024/11/01/how-to-evaluate-a-job-offer-and-ask-for-time-to-think-about-it/
UW-Madison SuccessWorks, accepting and negotiating your offer: https://successworks.wisc.edu/accepting-and-negotiating-your-offer/
inGame: Job offer is not a record in the game; carried as a call from an employer to a person with a deadline slot, tied to the person's traits (careful, impulsive). Needs: an offer record with a deadline.
